book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Likely Outcomes & Our Action Plan
question: Weighing the bull and bear cases side by side, what is our independent verdict across three time horizons, our holding action, and our exact capital allocation?

epigraph.quote: The hallmark of institutional underwriting is not predicting every tick; it is refusing to accept 1.08-to-1 odds at CMP when patience buys 2.28-to-1 odds at support.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Risk & Capital Allocation Charter

web_blocks.html: Our price-blind Pass 1 audit awarded Mondelēz International a COMPOUNDER_PASS business quality verdict with PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health. However, our Pass 2 valuation and tape check shows that at CMP $66.28, a grounded Base Target of $71.50 offers only 1.08:1 reward-to-risk against our $61.43 stop (0.85:1 at $70.42 consensus), while 6 distribution days and a US Downtrend argue against chasing. We therefore assign WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT ($63.35–$64.50).

web_blocks.html:
Three-Horizon Independent Judgment:
• Short-Term (1–3 Months): Neutral / Watch Support ($63.35–$64.50). Six distribution days in 25 sessions, 20% Confectioners breadth, and a US Downtrend (42.3% > 50DMA) argue against buying $66.28. Set GTC alerts at $63.35–$64.50.
• Medium-Term (6–18 Months): WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT. Q3 2026's operational inflection (+1.8 pp vol/mix, +380 bps Adj. GM) supports a grounded $71.50 target (21.0x $3.40 FY27E EPS), which clears our 1.50:1 hurdle only on a pullback to $63.35–$64.50 (2.28:1 R:R).
• Long-Term (3–5+ Years): Core Defensive Compounder. Emerging-market scale (40% of sales) and leading brands compound FCF steadily if buybacks stay within free cash flow.

Holding Action & Redeployment Plan: Our November 20, 2026 positions ledger confirms MDLZ is NOT_HELD (0 shares across Schwab and Robinhood; holding_shares_to_sell: 0). For new marginal capital, we assign WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT (CORE_ALPHA, TIER_2) and retain 100% in Treasury Cash until MDLZ pulls back into the $63.35–$64.50 support zone (0% at CMP $66.28; 0% to Outside Peer HSY in Stage 1).

Actionable Triggers & Falsification: Activate a 50%–100% buy tranche only if MDLZ tests $63.35–$64.50 on constructive volume with a hard stop at $61.43 (-4.8%). Abort the watchlist setup if MDLZ closes below $61.43 or if Q4 2026 vol/mix turns negative.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of truth. After stripping away the stock price to audit Mondelēz's business quality in Chapters 1 through 6, and then testing that business against its valuation, peer group, and Stage 2 chart in Chapters 7 and 8, we now put both sides of the aisle on the table and make an independent, unhedged decision.

First, let us steelman the bear case honestly, because a thesis you have not tried to break is a thesis you do not own. Bears rightly point out that Q3 2026's +1.8 percentage point volume/mix rebound was aided by -3.7 percentage points of European price rollbacks, while North America—Mondelēz's highest-margin region—remained flat on volume/mix. European chocolate still faces private-label competition, and on the balance sheet, $19.08 billion of net debt and $43.96 billion of goodwill and intangibles (61.5% of total assets) keep headline ROIC in the single digits (~9.36%). Moreover, 9M 2026 shareholder payouts of $2.8 billion exceeded $1.66 billion of 9M free cash flow by $1.14 billion (168.7%), extending the leverage creep seen in FY2024–FY2025.

Just as importantly, our Red Team stress test proved that assuming a 17.8% operating margin and $4.15 billion of free cash flow would exceed Mondelēz's 10-year pre-cocoa peaks (16.2% adjusted operating margin in FY2024; $3.60 billion peak FCF in FY2023) while ignoring $1.2 billion of ERP expenses through 2028. When we ground our Base Case at a realistic 16.5% operating margin and $3.55 billion of free cash flow, FY2027E normalized EPS is $3.40—supporting a $71.50 target at 21.0x, right in line with Wall Street's $70.42 consensus.

At CMP $66.28, a $71.50 target offers only 1.08-to-1 reward-to-risk against our $61.43 stop (and 0.85-to-1 at $70.42 consensus). Combined with 6 stock-level distribution days in the last 25 sessions, 20% Confectioners industry breadth, and a US Downtrend market regime, chasing $66.28 violates our asymmetry discipline. Instead, we assign WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT with a $63.35–$64.50 entry zone anchored on the 10-week EMA ($64.31) and 50-day SMA ($63.00).

From $64.50, the math transforms completely: upside to $71.50 expands to +10.9% (+14.0% total return with the 3.05% dividend), while downside to our $61.43 invalidation stop is capped at just -4.8%, yielding a 2.28-to-1 Base Case reward-to-risk ratio (and 4.40-to-1 in our $78.00 Bull Case). Across our three horizons, we stay patient in the short term, target $63.35–$64.50 for medium-term inflection, and rate MDLZ a Core Alpha compounder for the long term.

Because our same-session US positions ledger (November 20, 2026) confirms we currently hold zero shares of MDLZ across both Schwab and Robinhood (NOT_HELD, holding_shares_to_sell: 0), our action plan for the next marginal unit of US portfolio cash is clear: hold 100% in Treasury cash right now rather than buying at $66.28, set alerts for a pullback into $63.35–$64.50, and allocate 0% to outside peer Hershey (which remains stuck in Stage 1 consolidation at $175.48).

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: Why Tightening to WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT Is a Victory for Process
book_callouts.quote: When stress-testing your own operating margin assumption drops CMP reward-to-risk from 2.00-to-1 down to 1.08-to-1, you do not massage the numbers—you lower your bid.
book_callouts.text: By refusing to assume 17.8% margins above Mondelēz's 16.2% historical ceiling, we protected our capital from overpaying at $66.28 and set a clean $63.35–$64.50 trap with 2.28-to-1 asymmetry.

book_subsections.title: Capital Redeployment & Position Sizing Mechanics
paragraphs: Let us walk through the exact arithmetic of how we allocate our next marginal unit of US portfolio cash—say, a $10,000 to $15,000 risk-budgeted sleeve—across the three mandatory destinations: Shortlist setups, Outside peers, and Treasury Cash. Every dollar must be accounted for so that allocations sum cleanly to 100%.

First, we allocate 0% today at $66.28 to Mondelēz International (MDLZ) on our active US shortlist, because CMP reward-to-risk to our grounded $71.50 Base Target is only 1.08-to-1 against the $61.43 stop. Instead, MDLZ sits on high-priority alert for a pullback into the $63.35–$64.50 support zone (10-week EMA $64.31 / 50-day SMA $63.00), where reward-to-risk jumps to 2.28-to-1 and stop distance shrinks to -4.8%.

Second, we hold 100% of the marginal cash sleeve in Treasury bills today. With the broader US market regime in a Downtrend (42.3% of stocks above their 50-day moving average, 10 distribution days) and MDLZ showing 6 stock-level distribution days in the last 25 sessions, holding cash earns ~4%–5% risk-free yield while we wait for the market to bring MDLZ down to our $63.35–$64.50 shelf.

Third, we allocate 0% to our primary outside peer, The Hershey Company (HSY). Although Hershey trades at a similar 19.84x trailing P/E, its balance sheet carries higher leverage (1.11x debt-to-equity versus Mondelēz's 0.84x), its revenue base is far more concentrated in North American confectionery, and its stock remains stuck in a Stage 1 consolidation at $175.48 (-3.93% over the past year), capped by our technical timing gate at WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT until it reclaims its 30-week SMA ($177.01).

book_subsections.title: Monitoring Cadence & Quarterly Audit Checklist
paragraphs: While we wait for our $63.35–$64.50 entry trigger, our job is to monitor four non-negotiable numbers in Mondelēz's upcoming earnings releases: first, organic volume/mix growth must remain positive (at least +0.5% to +2.0%) without relying solely on European price cuts; second, adjusted gross margin must step higher from Q3's 34.2% toward 35.5%+ as lagged cocoa hedges expire; third, full-year free cash flow must hit ~$3.0 billion in FY2026 and expand toward $3.55 billion in FY2027; and fourth, shareholder payouts must stay within organic free cash flow so net debt stops climbing.

Let us also be crystal clear about our pre-committed falsification triggers. If Q4 2026 or Q1 2027 consolidated volume/mix turns negative again, or if Adjusted Gross Margin stalls below 35.5% and FY2027E consensus EPS slips below $3.25, then even a $63.35–$64.50 pullback would not be a bargain—because at the December 2024 trough multiple of 17.36x, $3.25 EPS implies $56.42 (-14.9% from CMP). In that scenario, we abort the watchlist setup completely.

At the end of the day, great investing is about stacking multiple independent edges in your favor and refusing to compromise on risk control. Here, we have a category-leading global snacking franchise with 40% emerging-market exposure, a verified Q3 2026 operational inflection, and a clean Stage 2 shelf at $63.35–$64.50. By holding 100% Treasury cash at $66.28 and waiting patiently for 2.28-to-1 asymmetry at support, we let price come to us.
